actions.reason: K6_C0001 has a coherent, candidate-specific molecular identity: a proliferation-high/oxidative-metabolism-low RNA program (E2F/G2M up, OXPHOS down, FDR 0.001) and a PBRM1-dominated mutation profile (18/18 versus 21/85, surviving both driver-panel and global correction). The confounder report shows only weak, non-robust technical associations (largest CT manufacturer Cramer's V 0.279, q=0.135), so no measured technical factor remains a substantial alternative explanation. The geometry-concordance report is the main limitation: native-distance alignment is near zero in CT, RNA, and WSI and only modestly positive in WXS, so the current boundary is not sharply mirrored in native geometry. However, the set is structurally cohesive (screen_candidate_k=1, no internal subdivision signal), the WXS alignment is directionally consistent with the mutation signal, and the known-label report shows only weak correspondence with established taxonomies, which is contextual rather than disqualifying. The full evidence positively justifies retaining this set as an independent discovery-stage candidate despite the modest geometric separation.

K6_C0002 has a coherent, candidate-specific identity: an immune-low/oxidative-metabolism-high RNA program (allograft rejection, IFN gamma/alpha, IL6-JAK-STAT3 down; OXPHOS up, FDR 0.001) and a VHL/PBRM1-depleted mutation profile (VHL 0/15 versus 56/88, surviving global correction; PBRM1 depleted at driver-panel level). The confounder report shows only weak, non-significant technical associations, so no measured technical factor is a substantial alternative explanation. The geometry-concordance report is the main limitation: alignment magnitudes are modest, but this is one of the sets with positive current-label alignment in all four modalities (CT 0.080, RNA 0.025, WSI 0.129, WXS 0.184), with within-label distances below between-label distances in every view. The set is structurally cohesive with no internal subdivision signal, and known-label correspondence is weak, which is contextual. The full evidence positively justifies retaining this set as an independent discovery-stage candidate.

K6_C0003 has an interpretable immune-high/EMT-low RNA phenotype, but the confounder report shows strong and robust technical associations with membership: tissue source site (Cramer's V 0.546, q=0.003), CT manufacturer (q=0.009), scanner model (q=0.005), reconstruction kernel (q=0.021), and slice thickness and z-spacing (epsilon_squared 0.261 and 0.265, q=7.42e-07). This is a material alternative explanation that the analysis cannot separate from the biological phenotype, and it is not merely nominal. The geometry-concordance report compounds this: native-distance alignment is near zero in CT, RNA, and WSI, so the current boundary is not expressed as a separation in those native geometries. The known-label report shows only weak correspondence with established taxonomies. The biological phenotype may be real, but the full evidence does not positively justify treating this particular membership as an independent discovery-stage candidate, because a substantial measured technical/acquisition explanation remains competitive. Dropping does not imply the observed biology is false or that these patients cannot participate in an accepted candidate in another run.

K6_C0004 has an interpretable immune-low/proliferation-low RNA phenotype, but the supporting evidence for independent retention is weak on multiple dimensions. The WXS report shows no driver-gene mutation phenotype (PBRM1 and VHL near rest-group prevalence, no significant enrichment or depletion), so the RNA phenotype is not mirrored by a genomic signature. The confounder report shows moderate, robust technical associations (CT phase Cramer's V 0.379, q=0.015; manufacturer q=0.043; slice thickness q=0.013; z-spacing q=0.015), leaving a material alternative explanation. The geometry-concordance report shows near-zero native-distance alignment in CT, RNA, and WXS and negative alignment in WSI, so the current boundary is not expressed as a separation in native geometry. The set-scope structural diagnostic confirms a single-cluster-dominated profile with a feasible k=2 solution that is highly unbalanced (4 versus 14) and has essentially zero silhouette, so no internal subdivision is supported. The known-label report shows weak correspondence. The full evidence does not positively justify treating this membership as an independent discovery-stage candidate. Dropping does not imply the observed biology is false.

K6_C0005 has a coherent, candidate-specific identity: an immune-high/growth-factor-low RNA program (allograft rejection, IFN gamma/alpha, IL6-JAK-STAT3, complement up, FDR 0.001) and a BAP1-dominated mutation profile (9/17 versus 4/86, surviving both driver-panel and global correction). The geometry-concordance report is the strongest positive structural evidence among the sets: current-label alignment is positive in all four modalities (CT 0.066, RNA 0.063, WSI 0.117, WXS 0.052), with within-label distances below between-label distances in every view. The confounder report shows moderate technical associations (tissue source site Cramer's V 0.414, q=0.009; slice thickness q=0.038; z-spacing q=0.014), which is a material limitation, but the consistent cross-view alignment and the independent genomic signal make a purely technical explanation less competitive than for K6_C0003. The known-label report shows a modest M-stage/stage-IV concentration in this set, which is contextual rather than validating. The full evidence positively justifies retaining this set as an independent discovery-stage candidate.

K6_C0006 has an interpretable mesenchymal-high/oxidative-metabolism-low RNA phenotype, but the evidence for independent retention is weak. The geometry-concordance report shows negative native-distance alignment in CT (-0.032) and WSI (-0.006), essentially zero in RNA (0.001), and only modestly positive in WXS (0.073), so the current boundary is not expressed as a separation in native geometry. The set-scope structural diagnostic confirms a single-cluster-dominated profile with a feasible k=2 solution that has essentially zero silhouette (0.00027), so no internal subdivision is supported. The set is the smallest (n=14), which limits stability. The confounder report shows only weak, non-significant technical associations, so technical confounding is not the concern; the concern is that the candidate's independent boundary is not positively supported by the multimodal geometry. The known-label report shows weak correspondence. The full evidence does not positively justify treating this membership as an independent discovery-stage candidate. Dropping does not imply the observed biology is false.
